$comment: Ground truth for pipeline-crm-app, a Lovable-shaped demo (Vite + React SPA, Supabase migrations, Deno edge functions) written for these tests. Holes are seeded on purpose; controls are done right and must not be flagged at Medium or above. H02 and H04 have policies that look fine in a dashboard; only the behavioural probe catches them.

holes.summary: Policy "Enable read access for all users" using (true): visitors without an account read every lead (names, emails, phones).
Select policy using (auth.role() = 'authenticated'): any signed-in user reads every other user's deals. RLS is on and a policy exists.
Own-row update policy with no column limit: a user sets their own plan to 'pro'.
Insert policy with check (auth.uid() is not null): user B writes activity rows in user A's name.
public.invoices never enables RLS: anyone reads, edits and deletes every invoice.
View without security_invoker: every user's pipeline totals are readable by anyone.
Deno edge function trusts await req.json() and upgrades the plan; verify_jwt = false makes it reachable by anyone.
Stripe secret key read from a VITE_ variable in browser code, so it ships in the bundle.
SECURITY DEFINER delete_lead(uuid) with no owner check and the default execute grant: anyone deletes any lead.

controls.summary: Owner-scoped policies for every command, (select auth.uid()) form.
Public price list: open read on purpose, no write policy. Static rules flag the open read; the probe sees no owner column and no write, so it may appear only as Low.
Edge function that checks the caller with auth.getUser() and keeps the Stripe key in Deno.env.
Browser client with the publishable key only.
SECURITY DEFINER trigger function with search_path = '' (the profiles file also holds H03).
verify_jwt = false for the Stripe webhook, which is right once the signature is checked.
